title: New England tour with Roberts and the end of Trent's band in Albany
summary: Roberts of Pittsfield books them through the Berkshires, Maine and New Brunswick until Trent's band disbands in Albany.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Yeah, that's right. Out of Pittsfield, Mass., wasn't it?

Out of Mr. Roberts. A fellow named Roberts out of Pittsfield, Mass., hired our band. And we played all through the Berkshires of Massachusetts, we played down on the Cape, we played through the Adirondacks, he kept us pretty busy.
What's the name of the place we played in Bangor?

IN Bangor -- in Bangor, Maine? We played at -- can't think of the name of that place in Bangor. I can't think of a place where we played in Portland. Portland, Maine, it was the Ricker's Ballroom in Portland, Maine. But we played all through the state of Maine, Mattawamkeag, Maine, we played up as far as New Brunswick, Woodstock, New Brunswick. We played Holton, Maine, we played Augusta, Maine, and Lewiston Maine. We played all through that country. And finally, things were just getting rough and rough, and got rough, we all came back to Albany, New York, and the band just couldn't any further, could it? Alphonso Trent's band just couldn't go any farther.
So we had contacted a fella named Chester Lane who formerly played in the band --
Chester Clark, who formerly played in the band, and in Cleveland, Ohio.
